title: Indian Literature and Schools of Philosophy

cards.b: UPSC asks about Vedic texts, Buddhist canon, Sangam works, and the six schools of philosophy. This is high-yield theory with simple pairings.

Vedas: Rig, Sama, Yajur, Atharva; Brahmanas, Aranyakas, Upanishads (Vedanta). Epics: Ramayana (Valmiki), Mahabharata (Vyasa; Bhagavad Gita in the Bhishma Parva). Puranas. Classical: Kalidasa (Meghaduta, Raghuvamsha), Banabhatta (Harshacharita), Kalhana (Rajatarangini, c. 1148, Kashmir), Panini (Ashtadhyayi), Kautilya (Arthashastra), Bharata (Natya Shastra).

• Buddhist: Tripitaka (Vinaya, Sutta, Abhidhamma) in Pali; Jataka; Dipavamsa, Mahavamsa (Sri Lanka).
  • Jain: Agamas in Ardha-Magadhi.
  • Sangam (Tamil): Tolkappiyam, Ettuthokai, Pattuppattu; epics Silappadikaram (Ilango Adigal) and Manimekalai (Sattanar); Tirukkural (Tiruvalluvar).

Tamil Bhakti hymns: Tevaram, Nalayira Divya Prabandham. Kannada: Pampa. Marathi: Dnyaneshwar’s Dnyaneshwari. Bengali: Chandidas, Chaitanya Charitamrita. Hindi: Kabir, Tulsidas (Ramcharitmanas), Surdas, Malik Muhammad Jayasi (Padmavat). Persian: Amir Khusrau, Abul Fazl (Akbarnama, Ain-i-Akbari), Babur’s Baburnama. Urdu: Mir, Ghalib.

Bankim Chandra (Anandamath, 1882; Vande Mataram), Tagore (Gitanjali; Nobel 1913), Premchand, Subramania Bharati, Mahadevi Varma, Sarat Chandra. Jnanpith Award (since 1965; first to G. Sankara Kurup). Sahitya Akademi Award (1954). The Eighth Schedule lists 22 languages; classical language status given to Tamil (2004), Sanskrit (2005), Telugu and Kannada (2008), Malayalam (2013), Odia (2014), and Marathi, Pali, Prakrit, Assamese and Bengali (October 2024).

Accept the Vedas. Six darshanas: Nyaya (Gautama, logic), Vaisheshika (Kanada, atomism), Sankhya (Kapila, dualism of purusha and prakriti), Yoga (Patanjali, Yoga Sutras), Mimamsa (Jaimini, ritual), Vedanta (Badarayana; Shankara’s Advaita, Ramanuja’s Vishishtadvaita, Madhva’s Dvaita).

• Buddhism: Four Noble Truths, Eightfold Path, anatta; schools Theravada, Mahayana (Nagarjuna, Madhyamika; Asanga, Yogachara), Vajrayana.
  • Jainism: Mahavira, 24 Tirthankaras, anekantavada, syadvada, five vows; Svetambara and Digambara.
  • Charvaka (Lokayata): materialism; only perception is knowledge.
  • Ajivika: fatalism, Makkhali Gosala.

Scholars like Debiprasad Chattopadhyaya (Lokayata, 1959) stress the materialist strand. Amartya Sen in The Argumentative Indian (2005) shows a long tradition of public debate and dissent. Orientalists tended to present India as only mystical; recent writers show logic, science and politics (Arthashastra) as equally old.

Classical language status brings funds for chairs and centres: in October 2024 five more languages were added, making 11. Yoga was inscribed by UNESCO in 2016 (ICH). Ideas of ahimsa and anekanta shaped Gandhi and today’s ideas of pluralism. The Constitution’s Eighth Schedule and Article 351 on Hindi tie to this literary heritage.

• “Discuss the contribution of the six schools of Indian philosophy.”
  • “Indian philosophy is more than religion. Comment.”
  • Prelims tip: Rajatarangini = Kalhana; Silappadikaram = Ilango Adigal; Sankhya = Kapila; Vaisheshika = Kanada; Advaita = Shankara; anekantavada = Jainism; first Jnanpith = Sankara Kurup (1965).
